title: Bands that played the Red Book and Bunk Johnson's uncle Willie Young
summary: Love lists the Alexandria bands that played the Red Book and rehearsed together on Sundays, and describes Willie Young, Bunk Johnson's uncle, as a faker.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about the Red Book. Oh, yeah. How many bands played the Red Book that you know of?
Let's see. Superior Band down there. Pete played with them sometimes.

Yeah. He played by Bronk Johnson playing the trumpet. And Harry Walker in Alexander. Well, they had some different bands around there. You know, they all played the Red Book. We was all connected together, you see. We had a big orchestra used to rehearse every Sunday. We just rehearsed over to them. And we'd invite all the musicians to that rehearsal, you know, a bunch of men. Every Sunday, there was Baby Lovey. he was a drummer. He was in Kansas City now, with Lee's band. And they had some bands around there, fake bands, you know, just fake music. They could play the same right, they hear them so much, you know. They'd play them just like the man that was reading. That was Bunk Johnson's uncle.

Yeah, Bunk, his uncle was named Willie Young. He was a violin player. He used to play violin, guitar and band. He was around Alexander at that time. Bunk wasn't that or Bunk was there. It was around 19, 8, 9, 10.
Was he strictly a faker, Willie Young?
